meta.title: Solti: Open-source task execution stack
meta.description: Build task-execution systems from composable open-source components for supervision, reconciliation, workload routing, agent APIs, discovery, and operations.
meta.imageAlt: Solti task execution stack with an engraved conductor and three flowing execution layers

hero.title: Task execution stack.
hero.lede: Starting work is easy, controlling its lifecycle is not.

stack.title: The stack you stop wiring.
stack.lede: Solti is an open-source stack for building task-execution systems. Compose Taskvisor and the SDK into the binary your product needs. Add Podium when desired work must be coordinated across agents.

items.body: Versioned Task resources with metadata, desired state, observed status, and watches.
Select a runner by workload kind and optional labels.
Commit desired state first, then converge asynchronously on the latest generation.
Apply retries, backoff, timeouts, cancellation, replacement, and shutdown policy.
Run subprocesses, native containerd 2.x on Linux, conditional chains, or application-owned workloads.
Expose the same Task operations through HTTP/JSON or gRPC.
Register agent identity, endpoints, API versions, and runner capabilities.
Add TLS, structured logging, Prometheus metrics, and live output.

stack.principle: Take one component or compose the stack. Your product keeps ownership of its workloads, configuration, deployment, and final security boundary.

components.title: Start at the boundary you own.
components.lede: Taskvisor, SDK, and Podium are independently useful. Compose them when the system crosses another execution boundary.

levels.title: Supervise asynchronous work.
levels.body: Own retries, backoff, attempt timeouts, cooperative cancellation, joined shutdown, and direct final outcomes. Queue, replace, or reject competing work by application key.
capabilities: Queue, Replace, or Reject by Key

levels.title: Build a task-execution agent.
levels.body: Accept versioned Tasks, reconcile the latest generation, route each workload to subprocess, native containerd 2.x on Linux, or an application-owned runner, and report observed state through HTTP or gRPC.

levels.title: Coordinate desired work.
levels.body: Run a control-plane service that persists desired specifications and per-agent rollout state, discovers compatible agents, and reconciles install, update, or removal across selected targets.

useCases.title: One stack. Different systems.
useCases.lede: Solti provides execution boundaries, not one finished product. Start with the form that matches the system you are building.

items.title: Own background work inside one process.
items.body: Give asynchronous operations explicit retry, timeout, cancellation, conflict, shutdown, and outcome policy without introducing an agent API or external control plane.

items.title: Turn one binary into an execution boundary.
items.body: Accept Tasks through HTTP or gRPC, route by workload kind, reconcile the latest desired state, and expose status, live output, and bounded history.

items.title: Keep processes and containers running without a cluster.
items.body: Build an agent for subprocesses or native containerd 2.x workloads on one Linux host without taking on cluster scheduling, networking, or storage orchestration.

items.title: Coordinate desired work across selected hosts.
items.body: Persist specifications and per-agent rollout state, discover compatible agents, and reconcile install, update, or removal instead of operating every endpoint by hand.

proof.title: Desired work in. Runtime evidence out.
proof.lede: This runnable SDK example commits a versioned Task, routes its container workload to the native containerd runner, supervises one hardened attempt, and retains terminal state and run history after containerd has removed the attempt.

lines.text: [shutdown] Supervisor and containerd cleanup worker stopped.

proof.note: This example is process-local. Podium holds desired state when it must outlive the agent. Native containerd attempts require Linux and a running daemon.

fit.title: Use the smallest thing that fits.
fit.lede: Use Solti when task execution is part of the product you are building. Use less when it is not; use a finished platform when you do not want to build that layer.

choices.label: Use local primitives
choices.title: You do not need a Task system.
choices.body: A future or fixed worker set needs no versioned resource, reconciliation, runtime status, or workload routing.
items: Retry one future → a focused retry helper
Join a fixed task set → JoinSet
Run one command on a schedule → cron or a service manager
choices.boundary: Move to Taskvisor when work needs its own identity, lifecycle policy, runtime control, or final outcome.

choices.label: Build with Solti
choices.title: Task execution is part of your product.
choices.body: Use Solti when your product defines what runs, selects the process, host, or agents, and needs one Task contract from desired state to observed outcome.
items: Lifecycle inside one Rust process → Taskvisor
Versioned workloads and agent APIs → SDK
Desired state that must outlive an agent → a persistent control plane
Process and container isolation → cgroups, namespaces, seccomp, capabilities, or containerd
choices.boundary: Your product owns the workload contract, targeting policy, deployment, and final security boundary. A control plane re-applies desired state after agent loss; Chain does not resume from a persisted step.

choices.label: Use a finished platform
choices.title: You do not want to build this layer.
choices.body: Choose a complete product when its operating model-not composable execution components is what you need.
items: Persisted workflow replay, step resume, or durable timers → a workflow engine
Workloads are untrusted or need strict tenant isolation → a dedicated sandbox
Ready-made cluster scheduling, service networking, and storage orchestration → Kubernetes, Nomad, or another platform
choices.boundary: This is a build-or-adopt decision. Solti can still provide Task supervision, agents, runners, and isolation inside that architecture.

commons.title: See the runtime as a system.
commons.body: Agent Overview is an Apache-2.0 Grafana dashboard for task state, lifecycle, API, discovery, and host metrics exposed by SDK-based agents.

openSource.title: Use one component. Shape the next boundary.
openSource.body: Start with a runnable example. Open an issue when a contract does not fit. Contribute a focused fix, example, runner, dashboard, or document when you know what should change.
